model.rationale: Hawaii's urban Honolulu seat leans Democratic by 13 points, incumbent Ed Case is seeking reelection with over $1 million raised against minimally funded challengers, and markets give Democrats a 96% chance. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or an unexpectedly strong Republican challenger campaign would be the only realistic path to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ed Case, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term representing this Honolulu-based district, which leans Democratic by 13 points. He has raised about $1.1 million and holds a substantial cash advantage, while Republican Adriel Lam has reported minimal fundraising. Minor-party candidates are also on the ballot but are not viewed as competitive.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Case. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 96 percent, consistent with a safe Democratic seat in a normal environment.
